chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man permits the private part of his slave girl to his brother.' He said, 'Yes, for him is what he permits for him from her.'

key_terms.لَهُ مَا أَحَلَّ: for him is what he permits

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a man permits his slave girl to his brother?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of *tahlil* (permission) regarding slave girls, establishing that the brother acquires the exact same rights of intimacy as the original owner. This ruling underscores the flexibility of ownership rights in classical Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the master's right to permit and the brother's acquired right to utilize. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the legal nuances of concubinage and marital permissions in the pre-modern era.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man permits to his brother, the private part of his slave girl’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, for him is what he permits for him from her’.
